title: Maurya Empire
capsule: The Maurya Empire was the first pan-subcontinental Indian state, founded c. 321 BC when Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda dynasty in Magadha with the counsel of Kautilya and expanded rapidly across northern India and into the Indus valley after defeating Seleucus Nicator c. 303 BC. Under Ashoka (r. c. 268–232 BC) the empire reached its maximum extent, encompassing virtually the entire subcontinent except the far south, and Ashoka's rock and pillar edicts — the empire's most precise territorial markers — attest administration from Kandahar to Kalinga. After Ashoka's death dynastic fragmentation accelerated; the last Mauryan emperor, Brihadratha, was assassinated by his general Pushyamitra Shunga c. 185 BC, ending the dynasty and beginning the Shunga successor state.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Mauryan heartland and main roads are well-attested by Ashokan inscriptions (rock edicts at 14 sites, pillar edicts at 7) and Megasthenes' Indica; peripheral regions including the northwest and Deccan frontiers are estimated from the edicts' findspots, leaving boundary zones substantially conjectural.
